title: coverage-preview passes vacuously on checkbox-prefixed [hard] criteria
description:
The `coverage-preview` gate (the `label-coverage` rule with `marker = "[hard]"`) passes **vacuously** when a container's success criteria are written as GitHub task-list checkboxes (`- [ ] [hard] REQ-NN: …`) instead of the bare marker form (`- [hard] REQ-NN: …`). The checkbox prefix hides every criterion from the criteria projection, so the coverage rule sees zero `[hard]` items and reports full coverage of an empty set. A breakdown can then clear the plan-time coverage gate while leaving real `[hard]` criteria uncovered.

## Background

The `[hard]` criterion marker is matched with a start-anchored pattern (`crates/jit/src/validation/engine.rs:1317`, `"pattern": "^\\[hard\\]"`; the same anchoring drives the `label-coverage` rule, `crates/jit/src/validation/serialize.rs:625`). A projected list item `[ ] [hard] REQ-01` begins with `[ ]`, not `[hard]`, so it never matches. `jit item list` then returns 0 requirement items, and `label-coverage` — which asserts every `[hard]` criterion has a `satisfies:` child — is satisfied trivially over the empty set.

## Discovery

Found while grading the `plan-from-import` scenario eval for `jit-planning-lead` (issue `41aa1b75`, recorded in `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/evals/results.md`). The scenario runner wrote the container's criteria as `- [ ] [hard] REQ-NN`, contrary to the plan-doc template's bare-marker prescription. Repro from that run (container `b3d778c0`): `jit item list` returned 0; `coverage-preview` passed exit 0; reformatting the criteria to `- [hard] REQ-NN` made `jit item list` report 6 items and the gate then failed, naming the uncovered REQ. Real coverage in that run was independently complete, so the eval scenario still passed on its literal rubric — but the gate verified nothing.

## Impact

The coverage-preview gate is the plan-before-fan-out guarantee for the bracketed breakdown flow used by both `jit-execution-lead` and `jit-project-lead`. A formatting variation a well-meaning author (human or agent) can easily introduce silently defeats it, with no error or warning. Severity is elevated because the failure mode is a silent false pass on a quality gate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Success criteria written as GitHub task-list checkboxes (`- [ ] [hard] REQ-NN`, `- [x] [hard] REQ-NN`) are handled so the coverage gate cannot pass vacuously: either the criterion is recognized (the checkbox prefix is tolerated by the projection/marker match) or it is rejected with a validation error that fails the gate. A container with checkbox-prefixed `[hard]` criteria and a missing `satisfies:` child MUST NOT pass `coverage-preview`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A regression test covers the checkbox-prefixed criterion case at the validation layer (a `[hard]` criterion behind a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` prefix is either projected or produces a validation finding), asserting the coverage rule is no longer vacuous.
- [hard] REQ-03: If the chosen resolution is "reject", the validation error message names the offending criterion and states the expected bare-marker form, so the author can fix it.

## Notes

Two candidate directions (design decision deferred to whoever picks this up):
- Parser/robustness fix (recommended primary): make the criteria projection or the `[hard]` marker match tolerate or explicitly reject a leading GitHub-checkbox token, so a checkbox-prefixed criterion cannot be silently dropped.
- Skill-prose fix (contributing, not sufficient alone): tighten `jit-planning-lead`'s plan-doc guidance so its runs emit bare-marker criteria. This reduces incidence but does not close the gate hole for hand-authored or other-agent input, so it should not be the only fix.

Discovered during epic `f2532a2d` execution; not part of that epic's scope (core validation behavior).
